title: Power series over a complete Noetherian ring are complete for the combined ideal
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $J\subseteq\Lambda$ an ideal such that $\Lambda$ is $J$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $d\ge0$, $R=\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ the formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and $\mathfrak a=JR+(X_1,\ldots,X_d)$. Then $R$ is $\mathfrak a$-adically complete.

proof.text: Apply power_series_mem_combined_ideal_pow_iff [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] to differences of series. Rewriting SModEq.sub_mem and Ideal.mul_top yields: F and G are congruent modulo a^n exactly when their coefficients at E of degree below n are congruent modulo J^(n-degree E).

Hausdorffness: if F is congruent to zero modulo every a^n, fix E and k, and take n=k+degree E+1. The coefficient criterion gives coeff_E(F) congruent to zero modulo J^(k+1), hence modulo J^k by antitonicity of ideal powers. Base Hausdorffness [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] forces this coefficient to vanish; coefficient extensionality [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] gives F=0.

Precompleteness: for an a-adic Cauchy sequence f, fix E and consider g_E(k)=coeff_E(f(k+degree E+1)). The coefficient criterion makes g_E(m) congruent to g_E(k) modulo J^(m+1), hence modulo J^m, for m<=k. Base precompleteness gives a coefficient b_E with g_E(k) congruent to b_E modulo J^k for every k. Assemble these coefficients as the actual function F(E)=b_E, a power series [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. To show f(n) congruent to F modulo a^n, fix E of degree below n and set k=n-degree E. Cauchyness compares f(n) with f(k+degree E+1)=f(n+1), while the coefficient limit compares the latter with b_E modulo J^k. Transitivity and the coefficient criterion conclude. Every coefficient limit is unique by base Hausdorffness.
Construct IsAdicComplete from the proved Hausdorff and precomplete fields. The statement and its Noetherian hypothesis remain unchanged. The proof does not require that hypothesis.

blueprint_update.statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and $J\subseteq\Lambda$ an ideal such that $\Lambda$ is $J$-adically complete. Let $d\ge0$, $R=\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ the formal power series ring, and $\mathfrak a=JR+(X_1,\ldots,X_d)$. Then $R$ is $\mathfrak a$-adically complete.

proof.text: Notation. Write elements of $R$ as $F=\sum_{E\in\mathbf N^d}a_E(F)X^E$, put $|E|=e_1+\cdots+e_d$, and set $J^m=\Lambda$ for $m\le0$. For $n\ge0$ let $S_n=\{F\in R:\ a_E(F)\in J^{\,n-|E|}\text{ for every }E\text{ with }|E|<n\}$ and $U_n=\{F\in R:\ a_E(F)=0\text{ for every }E\text{ with }|E|<n\}$; so $S_0=U_0=R$ and $U_n\subseteq S_n$. Then $S_n$ is an additive subgroup of $R$ (the coefficient maps $a_E$ are additive and $J^{n-|E|}$ is an additive subgroup), and $S_nS_m\subseteq S_{n+m}$: the coefficient of $FG$ at $G_0$ is the finite sum $\sum_{E+E'=G_0}a_E(F)a_{E'}(G)$, and each term lies in $J^{\max(n-|E|,0)}J^{\max(m-|E'|,0)}\subseteq J^{\max(n-|E|,0)+\max(m-|E'|,0)}\subseteq J^{\,n+m-|G_0|}$ because $|G_0|=|E|+|E'|$. With $S_0=R$ this shows that $S_n$ is an ideal of $R$. Likewise $U_n$ is an ideal of $R$ (if $a_E(F)=0$ for $|E|<n$ then every term $a_E(F)a_{E'}(G)$ with $|E+E'|<n$ has $|E|<n$).

$(X_1,\ldots,X_d)^n=U_n$ for $n\ge0$. The ideal $(X_1,\ldots,X_d)^n$ is generated by the monomials $X^M$ with $|M|=n$, which lie in the ideal $U_n$ (step 1); so $(X)^n\subseteq U_n$. Conversely let $F\in U_n$. The set $\mathcal M_n=\{M\in\mathbf N^d:|M|=n\}$ is finite. For each $E$ with $|E|\ge n$ choose $\mu(E)\in\mathcal M_n$ with $\mu(E)\le E$ componentwise (lower the coordinates of $E$ one unit at a time until the total degree is $n$). For $M\in\mathcal M_n$ put $G_M=\sum_{E:\,|E|\ge n,\ \mu(E)=M}a_E(F)X^{E-M}\in R$ (a family indexed by distinct exponents $E-M$, hence a power series). Then $F=\sum_{M\in\mathcal M_n}X^MG_M$: comparing coefficients at $E$, the right side has $a_E(F)$ if $|E|\ge n$ (the only contribution is from $M=\mu(E)$) and $0$ if $|E|<n$, which is $a_E(F)$ since $F\in U_n$. Hence $F\in(X)^n$..

$\mathfrak a^n=S_n$ for every $n\ge0$. ($n=0$: both are $R$.) ($\subseteq$) $\mathfrak a\subseteq S_1$: an element of $JR$ is a finite sum $\sum_k j_kF_k$ with $j_k\in J$, whose constant coefficient $\sum_kj_ka_0(F_k)$ lies in $J$, and $X_i$ has constant coefficient $0$; the condition defining $S_1$ concerns only $E=0$. Since $S_1$ is an ideal and $S_1^n\subseteq S_n$ (step 1, $S_nS_m\subseteq S_{n+m}$), $\mathfrak a^n\subseteq S_1^n\subseteq S_n$. ($\supseteq$) Let $F\in S_n$, $n\ge1$. Write $F=\sum_{|E|<n}a_E(F)X^E+F'$ where $F'$ has the coefficients of $F$ at the $E$ with $|E|\ge n$ and $0$ elsewhere; the first sum is finite. Then $F'\in U_n=(X)^n\subseteq\mathfrak a^n$ (step 2). For $|E|<n$, $a_E(F)\in J^{\,n-|E|}\subseteq(JR)^{n-|E|}\subseteq\mathfrak a^{n-|E|}$ and $X^E\in(X)^{|E|}\subseteq\mathfrak a^{|E|}$, so $a_E(F)X^E\in\mathfrak a^n$. Hence $F\in\mathfrak a^n$.

Injectivity of $\iota:R\to\varprojlim_nR/\mathfrak a^n$. The map is a ring homomorphism, so it suffices that its kernel $\bigcap_n\mathfrak a^n$ is $0$. Let $F\in\bigcap_n\mathfrak a^n=\bigcap_nS_n$ (step 3) and fix $E$. For every $m\ge1$, taking $n=m+|E|$ gives $a_E(F)\in J^m$. So $a_E(F)$ maps to $0$ in every $\Lambda/J^m$, i.e. to $0$ under the canonical map $\Lambda\to\varprojlim_m\Lambda/J^m$, which is injective because $\Lambda$ is $J$-adically complete; thus $a_E(F)=0$. As $E$ was arbitrary, $F=0$.

Surjectivity of $\iota$. Let $(y_n)_n\in\varprojlim_nR/\mathfrak a^n$ and choose $F_n\in R$ with $F_n\bmod\mathfrak a^n=y_n$. Compatibility gives $F_{n'}-F_n\in\mathfrak a^n=S_n$ for $n\le n'$ (step 3). Fix $E$ and put $c_n=a_E(F_n)\in\Lambda$. For $1\le k\le k'$, $F_{k'+|E|}-F_{k+|E|}\in S_{k+|E|}$, so $c_{k'+|E|}-c_{k+|E|}\in J^k$; hence $z_k=c_{k+|E|}\bmod J^k$ ($k\ge1$) is a compatible family, an element of $\varprojlim_k\Lambda/J^k$. Since $\Lambda$ is $J$-adically complete, the canonical map $\Lambda\to\varprojlim_k\Lambda/J^k$ is surjective: there is $b_E\in\Lambda$ with $b_E-c_{k+|E|}\in J^k$ for all $k\ge1$. Let $F=\sum_Eb_EX^E\in R$. For $n\ge1$ and $|E|<n$, taking $k=n-|E|\ge1$ gives $a_E(F-F_n)=b_E-c_n\in J^{\,n-|E|}$, so $F-F_n\in S_n=\mathfrak a^n$ (step 3), i.e. $\iota(F)_n=F_n\bmod\mathfrak a^n=y_n$ for all $n$. So $\iota(F)=(y_n)_n$.

Conclusion. By steps 4 and 5 the canonical map $R\to\varprojlim_nR/\mathfrak a^n$ is bijective, i.e. $R$ is $\mathfrak a$-adically complete. (The hypothesis that $\Lambda$ is Noetherian is not used: the argument holds for every ring $\Lambda$ complete for an arbitrary ideal $J$.)
